subject: Dedicated capacity ask: Zeppelin peak profile & SLO fit
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@zeppelin.com>
To: Karthik Iy er <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@zeppelin.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask: throughput profile + SLO

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Zeppelin Systems is close to a production launch for our customer-facing assistant and we need to lock down a Dedicated capacity proposal and SLO alignment. Attaching the workload CSV with per-endpoint percentiles and a short summary below.

Key facts:
- Use case: interactive assistant, median request ~90 tokens, tail (95th) ~320 tokens.
- Current user base: 120k monthly active users, expected initial peak traffic ~250 reqs/sec with short spikes to ~420 reqs/sec for ~5-10 min (marketing events).
- Expected steady peak tokens/sec (baseline): 250 reqs/sec * 90 tokens = 22,500 tokens/sec. Burst peak: 420 * 90 = 37,800 tokens/sec.
- Target p95 latency for token generation: <= 250ms (end-to-end for generation requests; customers expect snappy multi-turn responses).
- Security: will be on Dedicated (private VPC).

Ask: Can Redwood provide a sizing recommendation (initial reserved slab + burst policy) that meets the p95 latency target and shows headroom for the burst pattern? Also please flag any model tradeoffs (smaller/quantized vs larger model) and estimated token/sec per GPU assumptions.

Attachments: zeppelin_workload_profile.csv (per-endpoint breakdown), sample SLA draft.

Happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

—Sarah
Sarah Lim
Head of AI Products, Zeppelin Systems
From: Karthik Iy er <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@zeppelin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: throughput profile + SLO

Sarah — thanks for the clear profile and the CSV. Quick back-of-envelope and an initial recommendation before we validate with infra: 

Assumptions (runtime-optimized):
- Target model: orca-mini-13B-q4 (validated for instruction-following and cost/perf).
- Observed tokens/sec per H100 (our optimized runtime, batching & KV caching for median sequence length ~90): ~2,500 tokens/sec sustained.
- p95 latency target (<=250ms) maps to keeping queueing low; practical headroom target = 1.5x baseline demand.

Math: baseline steady = 22,500 tokens/sec -> raw GPUs = 22,500 / 2,500 = 9 GPUs.
Apply safety/headroom (x1.5) => 14 GPUs.
For burst capacity up to 37,800 tokens/sec, needed raw GPUs = 37,800 / 2,500 = 15 -> with headroom we land near 22–24 GPUs if we wanted to reserve for bursts.

Recommendation (practical):
- Initial reserved Dedicated slab: 12 H100 GPUs (committed). Rationale: covers most steady-state with modest extra for queuing; keeps committed cost reasonable.
- Burst policy: allow automatic burst to 20 H100 GPUs for short intervals (events), governed by pre-authorized burst pool (monthly cap).
- Run a 2-week canary with 12 GPUs + aggressive KV cache warmup and continuous batching to confirm real tokens/sec observed; if observed tokens/sec/GPU >2,500 due to effective caching, we can downscale.

Open questions for infra/chemistry team (cc Priyom):
- Verify the 2,500 tokens/sec per H100 number for multitenant Dedicated (private VPC) with Zeppelin’s request profile (short-lifecycle sessions vs long-turn).
- Confirm p95 mapping and queuing model for sustained bursts (we should simulate 10–15 minute marketing spikes).

Kimberly — can you draft the pricing anchor for a 12 GPU committed slab + burst to 20? Priyom — can you validate kernel-selection and batching assumptions and run a short simulator on the attached CSV?

If that sounds reasonable I’ll prepare a short slide with the recommended commit + burst policy and an SLA appendix.

Best,
Karthik Iy er
Sr. Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iy er <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: throughput profile + SLO

Folks — ran a narrow sim on the attachment (local sim, simplified queuing + batching model). Notes: 

- With the request mix and median seq=90, our runtime achieves ~2,400–2,700 tokens/sec per H100 depending on batching windows and prefix reuse. If Zeppelin’s workload has repeated prompts (templates), effective throughput can increase ~15–20% after warm cache.
- KV cache warmup is important. Cold start for new sessions shows ~30% lower tokens/sec until hot. Recommend an initial warmup plan: pre-warm common prefixes and prime cache using synthetic traffic during onboarding weekend.
- Latency risk: if we only commit 12 GPUs and a 10-min burst hits 37.8k tokens/sec, queuing could drive p95 above 250ms -> mitigation: (a) burst pool to 20 GPUs, (b) short-term model fallback to 7B quantized variant for marketing events (faster per-GPU throughput, slightly different quality).

Suggested alternative sizing combos to present to customer: 
- Conservative: commit 14 H100s (covers baseline + headroom) + burst to 22.
- Cost-sensitive: commit 10 H100s + burst to 20 + automated fallback to gpt-like-7B-q4 for event windows.

I’ll prepare a short table with tokens/sec per-GPU for the two model choices (13B-q4 vs 7B-q4) plus expected p95 mapping and estimated monthly costs (ballpark) — sending in a follow-up.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@zeppelin.com>, Karthik Iy er <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: throughput profile + SLO

Sarah — appreciate the profile and the quick work from Karthik/Priyom. Next steps from Sales & Ops: 

1) Pricing anchor: I’ll draft a 12 GPU committed slab price with an optional 20 GPU burst addendum and a 14-GPU conservative commit variant for your procurement review.
2) SLA + runbook: attaching a first-pass SLA (SLA-draft-v1.pdf). We’ll populate the canary checklist and cache warmup steps.
3) Engineering validation: Priyom — please share the tokens/sec comparison table (13B vs 7B) by EOD Monday so we can include it in the pricing packet.
4) Legal/procurement: Sarah, I added the HubSpot deal and a DocuSign link for an initial MOU — please confirm primary signatory so we can prepare.

We’ll also propose an onboarding weekend for KV cache warmup + synthetic traffic to ensure we meet p95 on day 1. If the customer prefers a lower committed entry point, we’ll include the fallback-to-7B strategy for marketing spikes.

Sarah — is Tuesday 10am PT good for a 30-minute sizing walkthrough with Infra and Solutions (we’ll bring the simulator output)?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA-draft-v1.pdf
